question: What foundation depth is required for the sign posts drawn in Figure 2A-2?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The evidence provided does not specify any required foundation depth for sign posts, and Figure 2A-2 does not depict foundation depths — it illustrates mounting heights (e.g., 5 ft, 7 ft, 17 ft minimums) and lateral offsets (e.g., 6 ft and 12 ft minimums). The only related requirement is a general performance standard that posts, foundations, and mountings must hold signs in a proper, permanent position; no numeric depth is given. Standards (mandatory): - "Sign posts, foundations, and mountings shall be so constructed as to hold signs in a proper and permanent position, and to resist swaying in the wind or displacement by vandalism." (No specific foundation depth is stated.) - "In rural areas, the minimum height, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the elevation of the near edge of the pavement, of signs installed at the side of the road shall be 5 feet (see Figure 2A-2)." (This governs above-ground height, not foundation depth.) - "In business, commercial, or residential areas where parking, bicyclist, or pedestrian movements are likely to occur, or where the view of the sign might be obstructed, the minimum height... of signs installed at the side of the road shall be 7 feet (see Figure 2A-2)." (Also above-ground height, not foundation depth.) Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 2A-2 shows only above-ground dimensions — mounting heights (5 ft, 7 ft, 8 ft, and 17 ft minimums) and lateral offsets (2 ft, 6 ft, and 12 ft minimums) — with no foundation or embedment depth dimensioned. [Image 7] Figure 2A-2 (page view) confirms the same: no below-ground foundation depth is annotated anywhere in the figure. Citations: - Section 2A.18 Standard §1 (p.60) - Section 2A.15 Standard §4 (p.58) - Section 2A.15 Standard §5 (p.58) - Figure 2A-2 (p.51) The evidence is insufficient to state a required foundation depth; the MUTCD material provided contains no such numeric requirement.
gold_answer: The MUTCD does not specify this information. A correct response should state that the requested value or requirement cannot be determined from the manual rather than inventing an answer.
